statements.quote: We release the platform, code, and dataset as a shared testbed for controlled studies of human–AI co-creation.
(1) a two-player, time-limited AUT chatroom supporting human–human, human–AI, and non-interactive baselines under closely matched procedures, with configurable LLM backend and interaction parameters;
(2) a pilot-tested dataset of 1,928 ideas from 62 participants with 6× redundant originality ratings; and

The platform is a browser-hosted, two-player chat application using free-tier authentication, database, and hosting. Environment variables control LLM backend, prompts, condition assignment, task items, chat length, and response wait times, so the platform generalizes beyond the pilot reported here. Source code and a live demo are available.

The non-GPT sets were drawn from Stevenson et al. [25], filtered so two independent researchers agreed on the extremes of the originality scale.

At edc61a3, constResponse.js contains 144 seed idea strings: 16 each for high, low and gpt under each of book, fork and tin can, confirmed by parsing the object in memory. has_texts_or_ideas=true refers only to these fixed stimuli, not the 62 participants' generated or curated ideas. Page 1 identifies the 62-person pilot as a separate file and names six planned/committed replication files: aut_subjects.csv, aut_idea_ratings_long.csv, aut_chat_messages.csv, aut_expert_validation.csv, aut_home_subjects.csv, aut_home_ideas_long.csv. None is in the public file listing. The PDF contains an analysis plan, data dictionaries and aggregate pilot findings, not participant rows. Printed CSV names and column definitions were not treated as inspected datasets; rows_checked and columns_checked are null.

PDF p. 19 says: 'The complete analysis script, environment lock-file (renv.lock), and R session info will be deposited on the OSF project page at publication.' No separate code file was listed. Public metadata links the restricted source project https://osf.io/tbdnw/ (listed separately).

CC0 1.0 Universal confirmed through the registration license relationship and https://api.osf.io/v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e96c/ (HTTP 200). The false outcome/text/assignment flags refer to participant records, not aggregate findings or variable descriptions in the plan.

Source project linked by the public z23v5 replication registration's registered_from relationship and by DataCite's IsVersionOf relation. It is associated with the N=205 follow-up; whether it also contains the c065 N=62 pilot is unconfirmed.

The OSF web URL returned HTTP 200 but only the generic OSF application shell. The metadata endpoint https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/tbdnw/, file-list endpoint https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/tbdnw/files/osfstorage/, and children endpoint https://api.osf.io/v2/nodes/tbdnw/children/ all returned HTTP 401 with 'Authentication credentials were not provided.' These initial checks were issued together; no further access was attempted. No login, account creation, access request or bypass was attempted.

File counts, contents, license, and presence of participant IDs, arm assignments, scores or texts cannot be confirmed. Restriction of this follow-up project does not establish that the target pilot data exist there, so it does not determine c065's overall status.

notes:
Checked 2026-10-10 02:51:35 UTC.

Read all 204 lines (34,306 characters) of the local markdown conversion and checked quoted text against the 8-page PDF. All 11 quotations match PDF extraction after whitespace normalization. The full document includes references but no appendix, acknowledgments, standalone data-availability statement, supplementary-file notice, or pilot preregistration. The conclusion's 'pre-registerable' wording describes a possible future use of the platform.

Source of record: the supplied arXiv PDF at the paths in retrieval.json. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07522 returned HTTP 200 and lists v1 submitted 2026-07-08; its abstract repeats the dataset-release claim but provides no study-specific data link. The DOI https://doi.org/10.1145/3803784.3816851 redirected to https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3803784.3816851 and returned HTTP 403; a direct publisher request also returned HTTP 403 with a 'Just a moment...' Cloudflare challenge. Stopped there. Publisher supplementary files could not be assessed; this is not evidence that none exist.

Both data/materials hyperlinks in the PDF were requested: the GitHub repository returned HTTP 200 (listed as a deposit), and https://co-creativity.onrender.com/ returned HTTP 200 with a 967-byte JavaScript application shell and no data links. The latter is the demonstration platform, not a confirmed data deposit. The form's only data_and_code URL is the same GitHub repository; data_url is empty. Thus each paper/form data link has been checked without duplicating the GitHub deposit.

DataCite title and surname searches yielded 2 and 56 records respectively. All 56 surname-result titles and applicable author/relationship metadata were reviewed. Only the target arXiv paper and the separate OSF replication preregistration were related; an article/preprint record is not a dataset. Zenodo's initial size=100 requests returned HTTP 400 because unauthenticated requests are capped at 25; retried with size=25 and received HTTP 200, with 0 title matches and 12 surname matches. All 12 were unrelated. Harvard Dataverse returned 0 title matches and 2 surname matches; both concern other work (technology transfer/firm-government engagement). OSF title filters returned 0 for the title and 0 for Hemmatian. This endpoint filters titles, not contributor names, so the verified first author's public-node endpoint was also checked: 10 public nodes, all unrelated. Generic Data nodes were resolved through parent metadata or DataCite relations to the author's label/diagnosis studies.

Stevenson et al. (2022), cited as the seed-materials source, is an earlier, different study. Its reference https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.08932 returned HTTP 200. Neither that prior study nor the N=205 replication can be assumed to supply observations for c065 S1.

Overall status is code_or_materials_only. The available seed strings and platform source do not support per-participant means, SDs or SEs by arm, analyzed sample/rating counts, or diversity of the pilot participants' texts. They cannot resolve final.open_items concerning rated-pool attribution, curated CON versus seed ideas, the HUM/GPT split of the carryover estimate, count discrepancies, or mixed-model arm counts. No empirical S1 table was publicly found and read. what_we_could_compute is therefore null.

The paper promises a dataset release, but the inspected public locations do not deliver the participant records. 'Utility results are available on request' is specifically a statement about utility results, not an explicit offer of the complete participant-level dataset; it does not justify overall status on_request. The inaccessible OSF source project is tied to a separate follow-up, so it does not justify labeling the pilot restricted. Confidence is medium because the publisher supplements and that source project's contents could not be inspected. No data files were saved; all remote material was inspected in memory.
